The examination of the course consists of two parts: 

- a **short essay** (1-2 pages) following the seminar on Day 4
- a **group project** on multi omics data, with presentation on **24th October 2025**.


#### Details on the group project
The goal is for the students to perform omics data analysis using the methodologies presented in the course.

**Datasets**

During the first day of the course, we will present three multi-omics datasets. 
For each dataset, we will propose two different objectives, for a total of six projects.

**Groups**

The students will be divided into groups of 4-5, which will be communicated during the first week of the course.
The students will be able to express their preferred dataset, but we may not be able to satisfy all preferences.

**Presentations**

All presentations will be held on **24th October 2025**, via zoom (the link will be communicated during the course).
The presentations will be organized in sessions: each session will center around the same dataset (*e.g.*, two presentations per session).

**Key points:**

- It is mandatory to be present at both presentation of your session. You are also welcome to attend all the sessions.
- Each presentation should last approximately 30 minutes, followed by 10 minutes of discussion (with primarily questions from the second group in the session). 
- You are expected to actively participate in the discussion of the other group in your session.
- Everybody should contribute to the preparation and presentation of their group's work.
- Suggested skeleton: brief background, explain which techniques you chose and why, present your results (figures or tables), conclusions, and limitations.
